messages:
maria-cs: Hey team, customer reported reranker returning weird values — negatives and values >1. They expect probability-like scores between 0-1. Pasting minimal request/response they sent. Anyone seen this?

maria-cs: Request:```json
{
  "endpoint": "/v1/rerank",
  "model": "redwood-rerank-v1",
  "inputs": {
    "query": "best ergonomic laptop",
    "candidates": ["laptop a", "laptop b", "laptop c"]
  }
}```

maria-cs: Response snippet:```json
{
  "scores": [-1.24, 0.11, 2.03],
  "meta": {"score_type": "raw"}
}```

maria-cs: Customer: "Why do we get negative/ >1 values? Is this a bug?" :thinking:

devon-ml: Not a bug — expected behavior in many cases. The reranker returns raw model logits (unnormalized). Logits can be negative or positive and aren't probabilities. If you want probabilities, you need to normalize (softmax).

devon-ml: Quick explainer: logits are score-space outputs from the last layer. For candidates [c1,c2,c3] you can compute softmax(scores) to get probabilities that sum to 1. Example (Python):```python
import math
scores = [-1.24, 0.11, 2.03]
exp = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
print(probs)  # sums to 1
```

devon-ml: Also check if your client code assumes scores are in [0,1]. If so, either do softmax or ask the API to return normalized scores (see samir).

samir-eng: We do have a convenience flag on the rerank endpoint: `return_normalized_scores=true` (server-side softmax). It wasn't widely documented in early SDKs — updated the docs yesterday. If you include it the response will be `{ "scores": [0.03, 0.12, 0.85], "meta": {"score_type": "probability"}}`.

samir-eng: Repro steps I used locally: 1) call rerank without flag -> raw logits, 2) call with `return_normalized_scores=true` -> probabilities, 3) verify sum(scores) ~= 1.

samir-eng: Note: normalized scores are computed per-request across the candidate set. If candidate list is large or you use batched requests, watch numeric stability (we use log-sum-exp under the hood).

maria-cs: Awesome — customer also pasted code that treated scores as relevance in [0,1] and then did `avg(score)` which caused their thresholding to behave incorrectly. I replied summarizing this and gave them the softmax snippet + option to enable normalized scores.

ops-bot: Created support ticket CS-8472 and auto-attached logs.

devon-ml: One more tip: if you need calibrated probabilities across queries (not just within a candidate set), you’ll need a calibration step (Platt scaling/isotonic) using labeled relevance data. Raw logits or softmax per-query are not calibrated across different queries.

maria-cs: Thanks — I'll send the customer the two options (client-side softmax snippet OR set `return_normalized_scores=true`). Also flagged doc update to clarify `score_type` metadata in responses. :+1:

samir-eng: I added a small note in the rerank API docs and opened a follow-up to log when `meta.score_type` is missing. Filed ENG-1214.

maria-cs: Closing loop with customer now. If anyone sees related CS tickets, please ping me.
